title: Clustered nulls reduce the evidence for a 629-day planetary clock in GLEs and X-class flares to p of 0.004 to 0.3; cycle 25 (2019-2026) events lean to the predicted phase but do not confirm it
abstract: Stefani et al. (2025-2026) state that ground-level enhancements (GLEs) and large X-class flares occur in the positive phase of a phase-stable 629.29-day beat of planetary tides. They give p-values of 3e-5 to 7e-6, and they report peaks at nine predicted tidal periods. Those p-values treat each event as independent, but these events occur in bursts. Also, the period was first found in the same GLE data. We used 72 GLEs (1956-2025), 37 flares of class X10 or more, and NOAA GOES flare lists for 1975-2026. A 0.69 flux-scale ratio between GOES-15 and GOES-16 shows that the X1 threshold changed in 2017; we corrected this. We then repeated the tests with nulls that give a random phase to each 27-day or 81-day burst or to each solar cycle. We reproduce the published phases (2.04, 2.96 and 2.58 rad against 2.01, 2.96 and 2.58). With clustered nulls, the fixed-period p-values become 0.024-0.051 for GLEs and 0.07-0.31 for X1+ flares. After a search of the 450-900 day band, no set has p < 0.05. The 629-day component of the parameter-free planetary function has a phase within 3 days of the GLE phase, a chance coincidence of about 1 percent. The GLE V-test against that phase gives p = 0.004 for 27-day bursts. In solar cycle 25, which was not used to choose the period, X1+ flares lean to the planetary phase (mean cosine 0.35-0.38, p about 0.05). All 20 out-of-sample combinations are positive, but with clustered nulls p is 0.03-0.34. Five cycle-25 GLEs give p = 0.22. The seven new predicted periods do no better than random periods (p = 0.08-0.24). Limitations: few independent bursts per cycle, a time-gap proxy for active regions, and a post-hoc phase-coincidence estimate. Cycle 26 can give a decisive test.

display.caption: Rayleigh significance at 629.29 d for each event set. Black bars use the published method (every event independent). Blue bars give each 3-, 27- or 81-day burst a random phase. Orange bars give each solar cycle a random phase. Clustering reduces the evidence by 1 to 7 orders of magnitude.

Per-cycle timing of GLE + S-flares (blue) and GOES X1+ flares on the old scale (orange) relative to the peak of the 629-d component of the planetary function s^2(t). The bars are 68 percent bootstrap intervals over 27-day bursts, and the marker size scales with the resultant length R. Cycles 20-25 are within a quarter period. Cycle 19 is not.

Mean projection of event times on the planetary 629.29-d phase (left) and one-sided p-values under clustered nulls (right). Orange bars are cycle 25, which was not used to choose the period. Pre-2019 GLEs pass, but the cycle-25 sets reach only p of about 0.05-0.26.
